b: My daily gratitude list made me ungrateful. Research confirms that thankfulness can backfire.
Psychologist Sonja Lyubomirsky found that counting your blessings three times a week can become boring.
Gratitude is best done while you do something else. Setting aside time from gratitude can be helpful. Practicing gratitude throughout the day is better.
Do Gratitude While Doing Something Else
Don’t put thankfulness on your to-do list.
When you show up for work: Appreciate the opportunity to contribute.
When you interact with people: Notice their strengths instead of obsessing over shortcomings.
When you lead a meeting: Recognize effort before pointing out what’s next.
When you have a tough conversation: Appreciate the person enough to tell the truth respectfully.
When you deliver feedback: Be grateful for the opportunity to help someone grow.
When you face challenges: Use past successes to bolster confidence.
When someone challenges your thinking: Thank them for speaking up.
Lead gratefully. Don’t schedule gratitude. Express it while you do other things.
Go beyond, “What am I grateful for?” Ask: “What would I do differently right now if I were grateful?”
What would change about your leadership if you did everything gratefully?
How to Win the Gratitude Battle – Leadership Freak
Note: Many enjoy keeping a list of blessings. My challenge for you is to bring thankfulness into the things you do every day.
